intro.text: Ramaco Resources, Inc. (the “Company,” “Ramaco,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) is a Delaware corporation formed in October 2016. Our principal corporate and executive offices are located in Lexington, Kentucky with operational offices in Charleston, West Virginia and Sheridan, Wyoming. We are a dual platform critical mineral company that is both an operator and developer of high-quality, low-cost metallurgical coal in southern West Virginia and southwestern Virginia, and a developing producer of coal, rare earth elements and critical minerals in Wyoming. Our metallurgical coal development portfolio primarily includes the following properties: Elk Creek, Berwind, Knox Creek, and Maben. wc.text: Accounts receivable were $73.6 million at December 31, 2024, which declined $23.3 million versus December 31, 2023 driven by the $31.8 million decrease in fourth quarter revenues year over year. Inventories were $43.4 million at December 31, 2024, which were $6.2 million higher versus December 31, 2023 driven by increased production. Accounts payable were $48.9 million at December 31, 2024, down slightly from December 31, 2023 due in part to variations in spending.

capex.text: The metallurgical coal markets are volatile in nature; therefore, the Company prioritizes managing its financial position and liquidity, while managing costs and capital expenditures and returning value to its shareholders.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During 2024, sales to two customers accounted for approximately 22% of total revenue.
No other customer accounted for 10% or more of our total revenue during 2024.
North American markets made up 33% of our revenues and export markets, excluding Canada, accounted for 67% of our revenues for
During 2024, sales to two customers accounted for 11 % and 10 % of our revenues, or collectively 22 % of total revenue.
During 2023, sales to three customers accounted for 15 %, 13 %, and 13 % of our revenues, or collectively 41 % of total revenue.
During 2022, sales to two customers accounted for 21 % and 17 % of our revenues, or collectively 38 % of total revenue.
The number of customers comprising the concentrations above is based on a threshold of 10% or more of total revenues.
Five customers accounted for 18 %, 16 %, 12 %, 11 %, and 10 %, of our trade receivables, or collectively 68 % of the Company’s accounts receivable balance at December 31, 2024.
At December 31, 2023, three customers accounted for 22 %, 19 % and 15 % of our trade receivables, or collectively 56 %.
The number of customers comprising the concentrations above is based on a threshold of 10% or more of total accounts receivable.
Sales into individual foreign countries equaling or exceeding 10 % of our total revenues for 2024 included India and Germany, which represented 11 % and 10 % of 2024 revenues, respectively.

The expectation of future prices for coal depends upon many factors beyond our control, including the following:
Our ability to receive payment for coal sold and delivered depends on the continued solvency and creditworthiness of prospective customers.
We are a holding company, and we depend on the ability of our subsidiaries to distribute funds to us in order to satisfy our financial obligations and to make dividend payments.
In some cases, we rely on title information or representations and warranties provided by our lessors or grantors.
Mining operations from time to time may rely on an expired lease that we are unable to renew.
We depend on our lessees to correctly report production and royalty revenues on a monthly basis.
Our ability to meet our payment and other obligations under our financing arrangements depends on our ability to generate significant cash flow in the future.
Our primary source of revenue is the sale of metallurgical coal.
Our primary source of cash is proceeds from the sale of our coal production to customers.
Our determination of whether or not a tax position has met the recognition threshold depends on the facts, circumstances, and information available at the reporting date.
Revenue Recognition —Our primary source of revenue is from the sale of coal through contracts with steel producers usually having durations of less than one year.
Performance stock units are accounted for as awards with a market condition since vesting depends on total shareholder return relative to a group of peer companies.
